title: Hawker stall rents to rise 40% next year, vendors say
text:
SINGAPORE — Hawker stall rents across the island are set to rise by 40% from 1 January, according to vendors who spoke to reporters this week.

More than 200 stalls have already closed this year, the vendors said, blaming rising costs.

The vendors, who run stalls at centres in Toa Payoh, Bedok and Jurong West, said they were told of the increase at a briefing last month. None would give their names, saying they feared losing their leases.

The last islandwide rent adjustment took effect in 2024. Stallholders said the years since had been lean ones, with the cost of cooking oil, gas and vegetables climbing through each of them.

A recent survey found that eight in ten hawkers are considering leaving the trade. The survey circulated among stallholders online, and its findings were written up by local outlets last month.

An official spokesperson was quoted as saying rents “will not be capped under any circumstances.”

The review takes effect on 1 January. Stallholders have asked for a longer transition period, and for the full schedule of new rents to be published before then.

Hawker centres remain among the cheapest places to eat in the city, and stallholders say any increase would reach customers within weeks.
